notes: Main-split ABox revision of a derived fact (15 queries), replacing the earlier Magna Carta edit (three models answered 'United Kingdom' to the premise check, and the edit had no stored neighbour for the related questions). Same shape as the geography template: the largest palace complex in the world is also the largest in the country where it stands, so 'the largest palace complex in China is the Forbidden City' follows from two premises that every model states, while the direct form is almost never written (14 hits for four wordings). The new value, the Palace of Versailles, has stored neighbours the edit overturns (it is in France; its Hall of Mirrors is in France) through the staging relations has_largest_palace and largest_palace_of (subproperty of located_in). Related near is the subproperty step, related far a transitivity through the Hall of Mirrors being in the palace; the premise-route query reaches China by a description (binding); the Treaty of Versailles question is a composition. Worlds: the Forbidden City leaves China (w1) or stops being the largest in the world (w2); the worlds are lopsided and kept unweighted. Known limit of the indeterminate query: under w1 it keeps the Forbidden City, so a model that never propagated the edit also matches w1; read w1 matches together with the direct and premise-route answers. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama). Review fixes: negation now reads "Is it true that ... not ..."; the related-near question asks whether the palace is in France (not the edit's own answer, China); the near unrelated query is the Forbidden City's builder, which holds in both worlds (its city would not hold if it left China in w1); the premise's evidence adds Wikipedia's sentence and two counts (Wikipedia words it as the largest preserved royal palace complex still standing; the premise stays as the common wording, and its check is not yet audited). Not changed: the related-far Hall of Mirrors question has the same shape as the geography template's Odori Park question (a stored part of the edited entity, with the one-country step in the worlds' shared assumptions).
